scope: Small file-bound guard/result metadata writer for a single stabilization run
cause: The immutable screenshot-guest-001 receipt reused the SHA-256 digest of the Debug 006 guard log. The actual screenshot guard log and private result files are still available; the audit does not establish how the wrong digest was copied.
contract: The tool reads both exact files and computes each SHA-256 from its bytes. It refuses missing, duplicate, or mismatched guard events, terminal unsafe/owned-process cleanup failures, and a raw pass contradicted by a nonzero child exit. It writes a new mode-0600 JSON file with exclusive creation. It emits only paths, hashes, bounded guard timestamps/exit code, a classified raw-result status, and validated build version/tree if present; it copies no child stdout or private result payload. It never accepts a caller-supplied digest or edits an existing receipt.
verification: The guarded unit suite passed, but merged CI 36280768692 exposed TS7016: the test's .mjs import had no declaration. A colocated .d.mts now declares the generator's exact input and bounded output types without altering runtime behavior. Light unit guards cover wrong-run refusal, independently recomputed digests for two distinct raw files, private payload omission, no-overwrite behavior, post-child cleanup failure refusal, nonzero-child/pass contradiction refusal, and nonzero-child/fail classification. Root owns the guarded compile rerun; this lane has not launched a browser, build, or test.
boundary: The generated metadata corrects provenance only. Raw result status is attributed to its file, child exit is attributed to the guard, and wrapper completion is explicitly unverified because the guard log emits RESOURCE_JOB_EXIT before owned-process cleanup. The record never claims overall acceptance or promotes an inventory case or defect state.
